title: With the setting off a shop sees no change
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, with one asset, asset 1.
custom_steps:
1. Open the work orders list.
  2. Click New Work Order.
  3. Pick customer A.
  4. Open Settings > Work Orders.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • No "Classification" chip shows.

Step 2:

  • The New Work Order window opens.

Step 3:

  • No "No Charge" checkbox and no badge show.

Step 4:

  • The toggle "Internal Work Orders" is off and no hint lines show.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-12295 (Story 13, Release day, seeding and migration)

  • Key Decisions: “No feature flag. Rationale: the setting under Work Orders is off by default, so existing shops see no change until they turn it on; that is the release-day protection.”
  • S2-N1: “If the setting is off, the New Work Order dialog shows no badge, hint or No Charge checkbox, and new work orders for flagged customers are billable. Open internal and no-charge work orders keep their classification, badge, orange header and category; they close as in Story 3 (S1-R10). Billable work orders offer no Convert to No Charge. While the setting is off, an open no-charge work order can still be converted to billable, and its category changed, from the menu; the Convert to Billable confirmation drops its second sentence. A customer change while the setting is off makes the work order billable whatever the new customer's flag; a No Charge mark survives a change to another regular customer.”
  • S1-R1: “Settings > Work Orders shows a toggle "Internal Work Orders" (Title Case like the other toggles on the tab), off by default, organization-wide like the other toggles, with the description "Lets you flag your own company as an internal customer and mark a customer's work order, or a single line of a billable work order, as No Charge (warranty, goodwill, comeback). Internal and no-charge work orders close without an invoice; their parts cost posts to the expense account of their category instead of Cost of Parts."”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
